adjudication.exact_delta: The local theorem proves irrationality for the pure-prime-power running-LCM channel (and merged pure-power ladder) with finite support size at least two, using all-one radix digits, bounded state clearing, and a separated right-special extension. The full smooth #269 shell has growing digits, so the interval-confinement/nonzero-form step does not transfer.
adjudication.proof_mechanism_comparison: The genuinely hard local step is the right-special-factor separation that produces a nonzero integer form after the bounded radix state is cleared; the finite checker only replays instances. This is a source-specific combinatorial realization inside a standard Cantor-series proof envelope, not a new general Cantor-series criterion.
adjudication.disconfirming_evidence: No bounded search found a verbatim r>=3 running-LCM theorem. The read Hančl--Tijdeman 2008 polynomial Cantor-series criterion is not an automatic match: its finite-memory coefficient hypothesis requires a coefficient sum o(a_n), while the all-one digit representation has a nonzero coefficient and the running-LCM radices are bounded. The exact two-prime comparison is source-matched to Bugeaud--Laurent by an explicit affine identity, but no argument transfers the pure-power result to the full smooth-number series.
adjudication.confidence_ceiling: Strong internal confidence in the pinned ordinary proof and Lean arithmetic core; strong framework attribution and exact r=2 Hecke--Mahler comparison; novelty for r>=3 remains unresolved. No priority claim.
adjudication.significance_rationale: This is one of the corpus's strongest positive #269 results because it isolates a complete mechanism and identifies exactly why the full shell is harder. Its value is explanatory and reusable even if later literature shows the r≥3 theorem is known.

r2_hecke_mahler_source_match.source_identity: Yann Bugeaud and Michel Laurent, 'Transcendence and continued fraction expansion of values of Hecke-Mahler series,' Acta Arithmetica 209 (2023), 59--90, DOI 10.4064/aa220323-18-1; arXiv:2203.12901v1.
primary_text_locators: Definition of F_theta and the lower Sturmian series, printed pp. 1--2 / PDF pp. 1--2
identity xi_s(theta,rho)(beta,alpha) = (1-beta)F(theta,rho)(beta,alpha) + beta^2 alpha^floor(theta+rho), printed p. 2 / PDF p. 2

local_two_prime_parameterization.theta: log(p)/log(q) = log_q(p), which lies in (0,1) and is irrational because p and q are distinct primes

exact_affine_reduction.height_identity: For support exactly {p,q}, H(p^m)=p^m q^floor(m theta).
exact_affine_reduction.local_series: Sigma_p = sum_{m>=1} 1/H(p^m) = sum_{m>=1} beta^m alpha^floor(m theta).
exact_affine_reduction.source_series: F(theta,0)(beta,alpha) = sum_{m>=1} sum_{k=1}^{floor(m theta)} beta^m alpha^k.
exact_affine_reduction.affine_identity: F(theta,0)(beta,alpha) = alpha/(1-alpha) * (beta/(1-beta) - Sigma_p), so Sigma_p = beta/(1-beta) - (1-alpha)/alpha * F(theta,0)(beta,alpha).
exact_affine_reduction.conclusion: Theorem 1.1 makes F(theta,0)(beta,alpha) transcendental; the displayed nonzero algebraic affine change therefore makes the exact two-prime running-LCM subseries Sigma_p transcendental.
